paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God shows up, and He makes Himself understood. The Holy Spirit fills Jesus' followers, and a crowd from all over hears them declaring "the wonders of God in our own tongues!" (Acts 2:11). Nobody had to learn a new language first, because the Spirit did the enabling (Acts 2:4). God doesn't want His wonders stuck behind a wall. He wants every person to hear them in words they know.

Now look at who was in that crowd. God-fearing Jews from every nation under heaven were living in Jerusalem (Acts 2:5), and each one heard the message in his own native language (Acts 2:8). That tells me nobody is too far away or too far from home for God to reach. And that includes you. The God who reached these folks is the same God who reached into my junk drawer, and I never saw THAT coming.

The crowd didn't all react the same way, either. Some were astounded and perplexed and asked, "What does this mean?" (Acts 2:12), and others just mocked (Acts 2:13). I think that's a gift to us, because it shows that honest questions are welcome, and asking them is a better move than laughing from the back table. So when God's Word is hard to figure out, keep asking, baker. And keep your apron on, because this story is NOT done.
